t.1.165.1: Arjuna said: What was the cause of the enmity between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha, who both dwelt in a holy hermitage? Tell us all of that.
t.1.165.2: This ancient tale of Vasiṣṭha, O Pārtha, is told in all the worlds; learn it from me exactly as it is.
t.1.165.3: In Kanyakubja, O bull of the Bharatas, there was a great king, renowned in the world as Gādhi, wholly devoted to truth and dharma.
t.1.165.4: That righteous-souled king had a son, known as Viśvāmitra, a crusher of enemies, whose army and mounts were abundant.
t.1.165.5: Together with his ministers he went hunting in the dense forest, piercing deer and boars in the delightful desert wastes.
t.1.165.6: Then he, worn out by exertion, eager to catch game and thirsty, came, O best of men, toward the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.165.7: Seeing him arrive, Vasiṣṭha, the seer who partakes of the best, received Viśvāmitra, the best of men, with honor.
t.1.165.9: Then the wish-granting cow of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, being told, "Grant the desires," thereupon yielded the desired things as milk.
t.1.165.8: With water for washing the feet, the guest-offering, water for sipping, and words of welcome, O Bhārata, he received him in due manner, and likewise with an offering of forest fare.
t.1.165.10: She yielded plants of the village and of the forest, and milk as well, and a six-flavored essence with the taste of nectar, an unsurpassed elixir.
t.1.165.12: Honored with those desired things, complete in every respect, that lord of the earth, together with his ministers and his army, the king, was greatly delighted.
t.1.165.14: Gazing at her, with her fine tail, ears pointed like pegs, and lovely horns, charming to the mind, her head and neck plump and long, he was filled with wonder.
t.1.165.15: Viśvāmitra praised Nandī, Vasiṣṭha's milch cow, and then, greatly delighted, he spoke to the sage.
t.1.165.16: In exchange for a hundred million cows, O brahmin, or else for my kingdom, give me Nandinī; enjoy the kingdom, O great sage!
t.1.165.17: This milk-giving Nandinī of mine, kept for the sake of the gods, guests and ancestors and for the sacrificial ghee, cannot be given away, O sinless one, not even in exchange for your kingdom.
t.1.165.18: Viśvāmitra said: I am a kṣatriya, and you are a brahmin whose means are austerity and Vedic study. Whence could valor be found among brahmins, who are tranquil and self-controlled?
t.1.165.20: You are established in power, you are a king, and you are a kṣatriya whose strength lies in his arms. Do quickly whatever you wish; do not hesitate.
t.1.165.21: Thus addressed then, O Pārtha, Viśvāmitra, as if by force, carried off that cow Nandinī, who shone like a swan or the moon.
t.1.165.19: Since you will not give me the cow I desire, even in exchange for a hundred million cows, I shall not abandon my own dharma; I shall lead away your cow by force.
t.1.165.22: Then Vasiṣṭha's lovely Nandinī, struck with whips and sticks and driven this way and that, lowed loudly.
t.1.165.23: Coming near, O Pārtha, she stood facing him, her face lifted toward the blessed one; and though she was beaten severely, she did not go away from the hermitage.
t.1.165.24: I hear your cry, good one, as you bellow again and again. You are being carried off from me by force, Nandinī, for I am a forbearing brāhmaṇa.
t.1.165.11: Foods to be eaten and drinks, dainties of many kinds, things to be licked that were like ambrosia, and likewise things to be sucked, O Arjuna.
t.1.165.13: She was long in six places, with fine flanks and thighs, broad in three places and compact in five, with eyes like a frog's, beautifully formed, full-uddered and faultless.
t.1.165.26: Struck with stones and staves by the fearsome troops of Viśvāmitra, I cry out like one without a protector; why, blessed lord, do you disregard me?
t.1.165.25: But she, Nandī, O bull among the Bharatas, harried by the force of those troops and shaken with fear of Viśvāmitra, went to Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.165.27: Thus, O Pārtha, when she was being assaulted, the great sage, firm in his vows, was not agitated, nor did he waver from his steadfastness.
t.1.165.31: Hearing those words, "Stay!", Vasiṣṭha's milch cow, her head and neck raised upward, shone forth, terrible to behold.
t.1.165.32: That cow, her eyes red with rage, her lowing a deep thundering roar, put Viśvāmitra's army to flight on every side.
t.1.165.33: Struck with the tips of whips and with sticks, and driven hither and thither, she, her eyes blazing with fury, gathered up her anger yet more.
t.1.165.35: Swooning with rage, she created the Pahlavas from her tail, the Śabaras and Śakas from her dung, and from her urine she also created the Yavanas.
t.1.165.34: Her body blazing with anger, she shone like the sun at midday, again and again releasing a great shower of burning coals from her tail.
t.1.165.36: From her foam she brought forth the Puṇḍras, Kirātas, Dramiḍas, Siṃhalas and Barbaras, and likewise the Daradas and the Mlecchas.
t.1.165.37: Then, while Viśvāmitra looked on, his great army was scattered by those furious hordes of many kinds of mlecchas, sent forth by her, clad in various armour and bearing various weapons.
t.1.165.38: Then each single warrior was surrounded by five or seven of them; and then, driven back by a mighty rain of weapons, the army was routed and fled in terror on every side while Viśvāmitra looked on.
t.1.165.40: But Viśvāmitra's army, driven back for three yojanas, crying out and stricken with fear, found no protector.
t.1.165.39: Yet not one of those soldiers of Viśvāmitra was then parted from his life by the enraged warriors of Vasiṣṭha, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.165.29: Have I then been abandoned, blessed lord, that you speak to me thus? If I am not abandoned by you, brahmin, I cannot be carried off by force.
t.1.165.41: Then, having seen that great marvel born of the power of brahmanhood, Viśvāmitra, disgusted with his warrior estate, spoke these words.
t.1.165.43: Abandoning his prosperous kingdom and that blazing royal splendor, and putting all pleasures behind him, he set his mind on austerity alone.
t.1.165.42: Fie on might, the might of the kṣatriya! The splendour of brahman is true might. Having weighed strength against weakness, I hold that austerity alone is the highest strength.
t.1.165.44: Having attained perfection through austerity and having propped up the worlds with his fiery energy, he of blazing might scorched them all and attained the state of a brāhmaṇa; and Kauśika drank the pressed soma together with Indra.
t.1.165.30: I do not abandon you, lovely one; stay, if you can. This calf of yours is being carried off by force, bound with a strong rope.
t.1.165.28: The strength of kṣatriyas is might, but the strength of brāhmaṇas is forbearance. Forbearance holds me fast; therefore go, if it pleases you.
